results.reflect:
Reflect (once, now that this unit of work is done): did any of these bite you
during it? If so, file it via `improvements:capture { kind, title, paths? }`.

Universal:
  - you retried a call, or the same tool errored more than once on the same input
  - you wrote a workaround for an awkward tool / API / doc instead of using it as intended
  - a task that should be trivial fought you past ~3 attempts on the same error class (the "web-search after 3 loops" point — the failure is confusing enough to suspect the tooling, not you)
  - lock or coord contention slowed you (a blocked edit, a stomped change, a presence/heartbeat surprise)

Pipeline (you ran the coding harness):
  - a validator failed on work you (or a peer) handed it — the validation contract is friction-prone
  - a reviewer returned work — the brief / scoping / convention that produced it is friction-prone

Bar: capture only a GENUINE, REPEATABLE improvement (a friction the next agent would hit too), not a one-off or a self-inflicted slip.
If nothing genuine bit you, capture nothing — sparseness keeps the queue clean.

specAdequacy.impactReport: EI-25948814148775899 is a behavior-changing bug that resolves no active behavior clause. D-012 expects a behavior-changing item to name the clauses it affects — This item has no source plan. Use the harness ad-hoc scope `adhoc-work-item-specs`: author an item-local clause with plans:set-specs while omitting `slug` and passing `planItemId: 'P-25948814148775899'`, then bind this work item and its proof with plans:bind-spec-evidence while also omitting `slug`. Shapes: plans:set-specs takes ONE object under `spec` (not an array) with at least specId, expectedRevision (0 to create), planItemId, behavior, behaviorClass and lifecycleStatus; plans:bind-spec-evidence takes ONE object under `binding` with at least workItemId, specId, specRevision, evidenceKind and evidenceRef, plus exactly one of `measurement` ({ schemaVersion: 1, kind, sourcePaths, ... }) or `sourceFingerprint` (or the ledger form { workItemId, specId, fromTestRun } that derives the rest from a test_runs row). Read the exact enum values with tools:find before the first call. Reported, not enforced (P-016 reports; P-013 turns this into a hard gate).
